 Global Pakistan LPG Crisis: Gas Supply from Iran Halted; LPG Crisis in Pakistan with Cylinder Prices Exceeding 10,000
 The disruption of LPG supply from Iran has led to a gas shortage in Pakistan, with cylinder prices rising above 10,000 Pakistani rupees in several cities.
 by Manali Sagvekar by Manali Sagvekar 
 25 Oct 2026 15:43 IST

 Advertisment 
 PakistanNews: The LPG crisis in Pakistan has become serious due to the disruption of supply from Iran. Reports indicate that hundreds of gas-filled trucks and tankers are stranded due to the border closure. This is affecting the availability and prices of gas in the market. According to the Pakistan LPG Association, around 7,000 metric tons of LPG come to Pakistan from Iran daily. Shamsul Haq, former president of the Gwadar Chamber of Commerce and Industry, stated that over 4,000 tons of gas were reaching Pakistan daily through the Gabd-Rimdan border post. However, he mentioned that this supply is currently completely halted.
 There has been a significant increase in LPG prices across various cities in Pakistan. In Balochistan, the cost of a 12 kg cylinder is around 7,000 Pakistani rupees, while in Lahore, it is reported to be 7,500 rupees and approximately 8,200 rupees in Skardu. In some areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the price of cylinders has exceeded 10,000 rupees. Lahore resident Farhat Abbas told Reuters that they used to pay 250 rupees per kilo for LPG; now they have to pay 500 to 600 rupees. Traders have expressed concerns that prices may rise further if supply disruptions continue.
 In addition to Iran, LPG is also imported from Iraq and Oman. However, reports suggest that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz are also affecting supplies from these countries. According to sources associated with Pakistan's Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the closure of the border with Iran is one of the main reasons behind the crisis. Hundreds of gas-filled trucks and tankers are stranded due to the closure of the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan borders, causing delays in gas reaching the market.
 Advertisment The rising prices of LPG have disrupted the economic calculations of families reliant on this fuel for cooking. Complaints of gas shortages and black market activities have also emerged in some areas. Irfan Khokhar, president of the Pakistan LPG Association, warned that if supply disruptions continue, the situation could worsen. He noted that the high cost of gas is also impacting the prices of other goods. If border transport and imports remain disrupted for a long time, the gas crisis in Pakistan is likely to intensify further.
 Short Summary:  
 The LPG supply from Iran to Pakistan has been halted.
 Hundreds of gas trucks and tankers are stranded due to the border closure.
 In some areas, the price of a 12 kg cylinder has gone over 10,000 rupees.
 Reports indicate that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz are also affecting imports.
 The high gas prices are financially impacting citizens, with complaints of black market activities emerging.
